title: The Golden Calf
lead: While Moses was on Sinai, Aaron made a gold calf and the people hailed it as the god who brought them out of Egypt (Exodus 32). The story became Israel's model of apostasy, retold in Deuteronomy 9, Psalm 106, Nehemiah 9 and Acts 7, and echoed in King Jeroboam's calves at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28).

sections.b: Later Scripture returns to the calf again and again. Moses recalls it in his farewell speeches, adding that God was angry enough to destroy Aaron (Deuteronomy 9:7–21). Jeroboam's calves at Bethel and Dan repeat Aaron's words (1 Kings 12:28), and the books of Kings call this "the sin of Jeroboam" for generations (2 Kings 17:21–22). Hosea mocks the calf of Samaria (Hosea 8:5–6; 13:2). Psalm 106:19–23 and Nehemiah 9:18 confess the calf in Israel's prayers, Nehemiah adding that God did not abandon them even then. In the New Testament Stephen cites it as a turning back to Egypt (Acts 7:39–41), and Paul quotes Exodus 32:6 as a warning to the church (1 Corinthians 10:7).
